items.titel: Ambition without alignment: Pollinators in the EU Nature Restoration Law
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Pollinators are essential for life on Earth. They enable the reproduction of most flowering plants and support biodiversity as well as food systems. However, their numbers are in great decline. Research finds a continuing decrease in pollinating insects each year. This article reviews whether EU Law is fit to address this challenge. First, this paper analyses the norms in the EU Nature Restoration Law (NRL) and the Delegated Regulation, finding that the NRL demands wide‐scale system change to comply with the targets set out. Second, it reviews what legal instruments and policies hold back these promises. Examples are the EU Pesticide Laws, EU climate laws, EU norms on light pollution, rules on Invasive Alien Species and, most pressingly, the proposed EU Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) budget. In the end, this paper concludes that the EU also has a responsibility to support the implementation of the NRL beyond interpretation manuals and soft guidance. It must fund, streamline and revise its own architecture, strengthening many existing EU laws to ensure coherence.

items.samenvatting_bron: Urban overheating is an increasingly prevalent threat to the liveability and thermal comfort of outdoor spaces in residential apartment areas. While urban green spaces can regulate microclimates and mitigate heat, there remains a lack of evidence on how design interventions can integrate environmental performance with human comfort. Following PRISMA guidelines, this systematic review synthesises 22 peer-reviewed studies from Web of Science and Scopus (2015–2025), selected from an initial set of 187 records. The review reveals that existing studies primarily quantify environmental parameters such as temperature, humidity and wind speed while inadequately addressing multifactor interactions and subjective comfort responses. To address this gap, the review proposes an integrated framework that links environmental metrics, human perceptual data, and climate-responsive design strategies. The findings further reveal that vegetation configuration, shading, surface materials, and spatial layout are key design levers, although their effectiveness varies across climate zones. Notably, this review offers a novel contribution by systematically identifying the interplay between objective microclimatic variables and subjective human comfort responses—an interaction largely overlooked in prior apartment-green-space research. items.titel: The population and the habitats of Common Swift Apus apus in the Brussels Capital Region
items.samenvatting_bron: This article presents the results of a survey of the Brussels population of Common Swift which was carried out between 2016 and 2018 under the programme "Monitoring of the State of the Brussels Environment" (for which Aves-Natagora has been collaborating with Bruxelles Environnement since 1992). The main objective was to improve our knowledge of the aspects of the habitat that are preferred by this population so as to improve our understanding of how the population may be preserved and its decline halted. Also a standardised protocol was developed for routine monitoring at regional level.The results have enabled the definition of the best sites for such monitoring. The densities obtained in this work are consistent with figures in the literature, suggesting that the methodology is adequate and that the figures obtained here can provide a useful basis of comparison for the future. Most of the colonies that we found were small. As regards habitat, we found that most nests were located under the cornices in non-residential areas (with mostly semi-detached buildings), located along narrow roads.

items.titel: eDNA metabarcoding reveals invertebrate diversity in the blackwater pools of southeast Queensland peatlands
items.samenvatting_bron: Despite harbouring a disproportionate diversity of rare and endemic species, the pyrophilic peatlands of southeast Queensland remain poorly characterized, particularly regarding their invertebrate communities. items.titel: Strategic implementation of green roofs for urban pluvial flood risk reduction: A case study of Milan, Italy
items.samenvatting_bron: The rise in intensity and frequency of extreme precipitation events is increasing the concern regarding pluvial floods in European cities. Urbanisation exacerbates the impacts of pluvial floods by affecting the infiltration process. Nature-based solutions, particularly Green Roofs (GRs), are promoted to mitigate these risks, as GRs can be implemented on existing buildings without requiring additional ground space. This study presents a risk-based framework to evaluate the potential of GRs in reducing pluvial flood risk in Milan by examining three implementation strategies, namely Water Depth (WD), Area (Ar), and Random Iteration (ITE). The framework integrates a hybrid hazard model, combining the empirical Curve Number method with a Cellular Automata approach using a hydrograph. The proposed hybrid approach enables us to link land-use-driven changes in flood volume to flood propagation. Extreme rainfall events with durations of 1, 6, and 24 hours were derived from ERA5. Residential building exposure data were extracted from OpenStreetMap and municipal datasets. Vulnerability was integrated within the framework using the INSYDE model, complemented by four additional vulnerability functions for sensitivity analysis. Results indicate that GRs can effectively reduce pluvial flood-induced losses, with reductions of 16-69% across different rainfall durations. items.titel: Review article: Mountain flash floods: from hazard formation to disaster risk reduction pathways
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract. Flash floods in mountainous regions are becoming more frequent and destructive under climate warming, yet cross-regional understanding of their triggering mechanisms, cascading impacts, and governance remains fragmented. This review synthesises 1,967 studies published during 2000–2025 to establish a globally comparable baseline of mountain flash-flood research. By integrating bibliometric and topic analyses with qualitative synthesis, we reveal pronounced geographical and thematic imbalances, with research concentrated in Europe and Asia. At the same time, many high-risk mountain regions in Africa and South America remain overlooked. Across regions, flash-flood initiation and impacts are shown to be strongly state-dependent and coupled, emerging from interactions between storm intensity, duration and spatial concentration, antecedent hydrological conditions, and hillslope-channel connectivity. This coupling helps explain why fixed rainfall thresholds are difficult to generalise and highlights the need for dynamic, multi-source early-warning approaches. Comparing evidence on early warning, structural protection, and Nature-Based Solutions, the review shows that cascading processes dominate risk management challenges. items.titel: Understanding public preferences for urban wildflower meadows
items.samenvatting_bron: Accelerating urbanisation challenges biodiversity and human wellbeing, demanding effective urban nature-based solutions. Urban wildflower meadows are increasingly popular interventions that may offer biodiversity and wellbeing benefits. However, realising their potential depends on public support, which requires robust evidence on which meadow design attributes the public prefers and values most. We conducted a choice experiment with urban greenspace users across three UK cities to quantify willingness-to-pay (WTP) for some of the key characteristics of wildflower meadows in public parks, namely flower colour diversity, native species composition, plant species richness, and pollinator habitat quality. Het afgelopen jaar is dit onderzoek geactualiseerd om een actueel beeld te krijgen van de kosten van een openbare dienstver- plichting (public service obligation, PSO) op de Bovenwindse Eilanden. In deze brief wordt de Kamer geïnformeerd over dit onderzoek. Aanleiding onderzoeken In 2021 is het aandeelhouderschap van de beleidsdeelneming in Winair geëvalueerd2. Uit deze evaluatie is geconcludeerd dat het aandeelhouder- schap niet het meest geschikte instrument is om een betaalbare en betrouwbare bereikbaarheid van de bijzondere Nederlandse gemeenten Saba en Sint Eustatius te borgen. In deze evaluatie is tevens gemeld dat het kabinet een PSO als alternatief instrument onderzoekt. Een wijziging van de Luchtvaartwet BES om een PSO mogelijk te maken ligt op dit moment voor in de Tweede Kamer. We are determined to prevent smugglers from challenging the integrity of the Union ’s external borders. We recognise that the recent ruling of the Spanish Supreme Court has been used to trigger this attack and abuse our migration and asylum system. document.tekst_begin: 1 ELA september 2026 Inleiding Een krachtige strafrechtelijke aanpak van geweld en agressie tegen functionarissen met een publieke taak blijft essentieel. Het idee achter de Veilige Publieke Taak (VPT) is dat functionarissen die zich professioneel inzetten voor onze rechtsstaat erop moeten kunnen rekenen dat zij hun werk veilig en ongehinderd kunnen doen. Het Openbaar Ministerie (OM) en de politie hebben ten behoeve van de strafrechtelijke aanpak van agressie en geweld opsporings- en vervolgingsafspraken gemaakt, de Eenduidige Landelijke Afspraken (ELA). De vorige versie van de ELA gold sinds 2010. In 2025 heeft de minister van Justitie en Veiligheid aan de Kamer toegezegd om samen met de politie en het OM de ELA te herzien en om daarbij de bevindingen uit de praktijk en de verschillende evaluaties te betrekken.1 Hieruit is deze nieuwe versie van de ELA voortgekomen. Doel Het doel van deze afspraken is een eenduidige, effectieve en snelle afhandeling van agressie en geweld tegen functionarissen met een publieke taak door de politie en het OM. Berendsen kst-21501-02-3460 ISSN 0921 - 7371 ’s-Gravenhage 2026 Tweede Kamer, vergaderjaar 2025–2026, 21 501-02, nr. 3460 1 VERSLAG RAAD ALGEMENE ZAKEN VAN 14 JULI 2026 De Raad Algemene Zaken (RAZ) vond plaats in Brussel op dinsdag 14 juli jl. document.tekst_begin: Position paper Rutgers gesprek over medische desinformatie Rutgers zet zich, als kennis- en expertisecentrum seksualiteit, al sinds de jaren zestig in voor het bieden van betrouwbare en volledige informatie over relaties en seksualiteit. Dit doen we o.a. via publiekscampagnes, websites en deskundigheidsbevordering van professionals. De afgelopen jaren zijn we, met de opkomst van sociale media en AI, voor nieuwe uitdagingen komen te staan. Online zoeken naar informatie is niet slecht, maar wordt een probleem wanneer deze bronnen eenzijdige, onjuiste, onvolledige of sturende informatie bevatten. Wij maken ons zorgen over de invloed die misinformatie kan hebben op de mate waarin iemand goed geïnformeerd keuzes kan maken, bijvoorbeeld over anticonceptie, zwangerschap en kinderwens. De impact van misinformatie bereikt ook de spreekkamer. Daar zien zorgverleners dat mensen vragen, zorgen en overtuigingen meenemen die zij via (sociale) media, influencers, ai -chatbots en online platforms hebben opgedaan. document.tekst_begin: Aanleiding Op vrijdagmiddag 25 september jl. heeft het NCSC vertrouwelijk haar doelgroep geïnformeerd over twee ernstige kwetsbaarheden in Citrix Netscaler. Citrix Netscaler zorgt ervoor dat websites en applicaties snel en betrouwbaar bereikbaar blijven. Dit wordt gebruikt om thuiswerken te faciliteren. De kwetsbaarheden werden/worden actief misbruikt, en de kans op misbruik neemt toe naarmate de bekendheid van de kwetsbaarheden toeneemt. Met deze Kamerbrief wordt de Kamer geïnformeerd over de situatie en de genomen maatregelen om de impact te beperken. Geadviseerd besluit Kennisnemen van de inhoud van deze nota en akkoord gaan met verzending van de Kamerbrief. Kern Afgelopen vrijdag heeft NCSC gemeld dat er ernstige kwetsbaarheden zijn in Citrix. In de brief wordt toegelicht welke acties in gang zijn gezet binnen de rijksoverheid en wat de stand van zaken op dit moment is. Motivering In de openbaar gemaakte versie van deze nota zijn alle persoonsgegevens van ambtenaren geanonimiseerd. items.titel: Procedimenti ambientali complessi e tutela europea della biodiversità: deroghe per le specie protette, termini di impugnazione e accesso alla giustizia
items.samenvatting_bron: This article examines, in the light of the Court of Justice’s judgment in Drumakilla, the relationship between the strict protection of animal species under the Habitats Directive, the environmental impact assessment process and national rules governing judicial review. The Court held that EU law does not preclude a Member State from treating a derogation granted under Article 16 of the Habitats Directive as an autonomous act subject to a three-month limitation period, even where that period may expire before final development consent is issued. Such procedural autonomy remains subject to equivalence and effectiveness, actual or reasonable knowledge of both the operative part and the reasons of the decision, and foreseeability of the applicable remedy. The judgment departs from Advocate General Medina’s integrated approach, under which the period could not expire before final consent. The analysis shows that the Court separates the substantive unity of environmental decision-making from the procedural autonomy of its component acts and insufficiently addresses the cumulative burden generated by multiple authorisations and proceedings. The comparison with French, German and Italian law points towards a model of procedural integration without mandatory institutional fusion.

items.titel: evealing the stream, reconnecting the city: the impact of Zürich’s bachkonzept on pedestrian networks and active living
items.samenvatting_bron: The burial and culverting of urban streams during twentieth-century urbanization severed the relationship between natural hydrological systems and the built environment, resulting in the loss of critical ecosystem services. While urban waterways are often perceived as barriers to movement, their reinstatement at ground level through ‘stream daylighting’ presents an opportunity to reconfigure urban form in ways that support both ecological and social resilience. This study investigates the impact of stream daylighting on pedestrian network connectivity in Zurich, Switzerland. Using a comparative spatial analysis of pre-and post-daylighting conditions, the study employs a configurational approach based on metric reach within a GIS environment. Historic georeferenced maps from 1984 were digitized and compared with 2020 open-access spatial data to assess changes in route network connectivity. These quantitative findings are complemented by photographic documentation to evaluate the urban design interventions accompanying daylighting projects. Contrary to the assumption that reinstating streams at ground level disrupts connectivity, the results reveal that daylighting in Zurich often enhances pedestrian accessibility. This is achieved through integrated urban design strategies, such as the inclusion of footbridges and the creation of new public spaces, which maintain or improve existing route networks. document.tekst_begin: Position paper LECK | Rondetafelgesprek Kindermishandeling 28 oktober 2026 | pagina 1 POSITION PAPER LECK Rondetafelgesprek Kindermishandeling 28 oktober 2026 Aanleiding: op 28 oktober 2026 organiseert de vaste commissie VWS een rondetafelgesprek over kindermishandeling, met als doel om van deskundigen en ervaringsdeskundigen te horen wat helpt om kindermishandeling tegen te gaan: wat is kinderen overkomen, hoe is er ingegrepen en wat had beter gekund? Het Landelijk Expertise Centrum Kindermishandeling (LECK) deelt in dit position paper de ervaringen die kinderartsen, forensisch artsen en kinderradiologen hebben met kinderen die zich met letsel of lichamelijke symptomen bij een medisch professional presenteren. Ons standpunt: Bij vermoedens van kindermishandeling moet het kind centraal staan in het onderzoek, dat zo snel en zorgvuldig mogelijk moet worden ingezet. document.tekst_begin: Onmisbaar bij Post-Covid en PAIS: kennis, maatwerk en passende begeleiding 1 Vanaf 2022 krijgt UWV in toenemende mate te maken met WIA-beoordelingen van cliënten met Post-Covid, met name in de sector Zorg en Welzijn. Bij Post-Covid wordt in 85% van de gevallen een WIA-uitkering toegekend, tegenover circa 70% gemiddeld. Het merendeel (>50%) blijkt volledig arbeidsongeschikt (WGA 80-100% of IVA). Sinds 2025 neemt de WIA-instroom van mensen met Post-Covid af. Aantal toegekende WIA-uitkeringen van personen tot 60 jaar in de sectoren zorg en welzijn, openbaar bestuur en onderwijs naar ziektebeeld (hoofddiagnose), 1e halfjaar 2022–1e halfjaar 2025*1 * De diagnose is deels geschat. In het eerste halfjaar van 2024 is de diagnose van 9% van de WIA-instroom namelijk nog niet bekend. In het eerste halfjaar van 2025 gaat het om 18%. De instroom met onbekende diagnose is naar rato verdeeld over de bekende diagnoses. document.tekst_begin: Deze position paper is geschreven voor het rondetafelgesprek Post-Covid / PAIS in de Commissie Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport van de Tweede Kamer op 26 oktober 2026 Geef ons de kans op een toekomst Introductie Wij zijn jongeren met long covid. Waar ons leven ooit gevuld was met school, werk, sport, vrienden en toekomstdromen, is nu een paar uur werken of onderwijs volgen vaak al te veel. Terwijl anderen, en misschien u ook, op onze leeftijd samen of op zichzelf woonden, diploma's haalden, promotie maakten, en kinderen kregen, zetten wij noodgedwongen stappen terug. Long covid beperkt ons in het volgen van een opleiding en onze stap naar volwassenheid. Sommigen van ons kunnen helemaal niet naar school, studie of werk, anderen een paar uur of alleen onder zeer specifieke omstandigheden. Wij willen graag bijdragen aan de samenleving, op de manier die onze gezondheid toelaat. Momenteel vinden we echter maar beperkt onze weg naar de arbeidsmarkt en de sociale zekerheid, stoppen wij met onze opleiding of baan en zijn we afhankelijk van thuis- en mantelzorg. De Post-COVID expertisecentra voor kinderen Het UMC Utrecht heeft samen met het Amsterdam UMC een post-COVID expertisecentrum opgericht voor kinderen met langdurige klachten na COVID-19. Deze centra richten zich specifiek op kinderen en jongeren met langdurige klachten na een COVID-19-infectie. Sinds de start van deze expertisecentra op 1 februari 2026 zijn er landelijk ruim 300 kinderen gezien. Kinderen worden onderzocht door multidisciplinaire teams, die de zorg afstemmen op de klachten en behoeften van iedere patiënt. De Ierse Minister van Landbouw, Voedsel en Maritieme Zaken, Martin Heydon, zat de vergadering voor. Timmy Dooley, de Ierse Staatssecretaris voor Visserij en Maritieme Zaken, was ook aanwezig. Het thema van de informele Visserijraad was generatievernieuwing in de visserijsector. Het Ierse voorzitterschap opende de vergadering door te benadrukken dat generatievernieuwing belangrijk is om toekomstige generaties van voedsel uit onze eigen zeeën te kunnen voorzien. Daarbij benadrukte de voorzitter het belang van een aantrekkelijke, winstgevende en veilige sector. Naast andere uitdagingen, constateerde het Ierse voorzitterschap dat klimaatverandering en stijgende brandstofkosten als gevolg van conflicten in het Midden-Oosten een grote impact hebben op de sector. Door de commissie wordt onder meer aanbevolen te onderzoeken of de intro- ductie van een mededingingskader zou kunnen bijdragen aan sterkere eilandeconomieën en lagere prijzen. Toegezegd is dat mijn ministerie samen met de Openbare Lichamen zou verkennen welke verbeteringen in dit kader mogelijk zijn. Naar aanleiding hiervan heeft Economisch Bureau Amsterdam (hierna: EBA) in opdracht van mijn ministerie een advies uitgebracht over de mogelijkheden om mededingings- en consumentenbeschermingsbeleid in meerdere gradaties en fasering in te voeren op de BES-eilanden. Het lokale bestuur van deze eilanden was vertegenwoordigd in een klankbord- groep die dit onderzoek heeft begeleid.

Is sprake van een heldere probleemstelling? Woningcorporaties vervullen een essentiële maatschappelijke taak bij het waarborgen van voldoende, betaalbare en passende huisvesting in Nederland. Het kabinet erkent de onmisbare rol van woningcorporaties, met name in de huidige wooncrisis, en heeft zich in het regeerakkoord volledig gecommitteerd aan de Nationale Prestatieafspraken (NPA). De NPA bevatten afspraken met woningcorporaties over hun bijdrage aan de volkshuisvestelijke opgaven voor de komende jaren. Om een bijdrage te leveren aan een grotere financiële slagkracht van de corporatiesector om uitvoering te kunnen geven aan de NPA is in het regeerakkoord een pakket aan maatregelen afgesproken. De voorgestelde uitzondering voor woningcorporaties ten aanzien van de DAEB-activiteiten in de generieke renteaftrekbeperking (de earningsstrippingmaatregel) is een van deze maatregelen. 2. items.titel: Delineating and Mapping Green Infrastructure Systems: A Case Study of Central Wuhan, China
items.samenvatting_bron: Green infrastructure (GI) is widely recognized as an essential solution for addressing urban environmental issues such as pollution, flooding, urban heat islands, and climate change. However, despite its increasing importance, a unified definition and classification system for green infrastructure has yet to be established. This study selected the central urban area of Wuhan as the study area, where extensive urban development coexists with diverse ecological spaces. Based on web map AOI data, high-resolution remote sensing imagery (approximately meter-level spatial resolution), the Third National Land Survey, and urban planning databases, a green infrastructure classification system encompassing natural, semi-natural and artificial elements was identified and constructed through multisource spatial data integration and deep learning-assisted image interpretation. Landscape indices were used to measure the connectivity and fragmentation of green infrastructure landscapes within the city, including metrics such as contagion, Shannon diversity index, and edge density. Finally, the Minimum Cumulative Resistance (MCR) model and the gravity model were employed to construct the green infrastructure network. The results identified 6974 green infrastructure elements, which were classified into two categories and 15 subcategories. items.titel: From cemeteries to ecological memorial landscapes: the rise of green and conservation burial grounds and its opportunities for urban planning
items.samenvatting_bron: The article conducts an interpretative review of contemporary scientific literature (2000–2026) to analyse the environmental aspects of conventional funeral practices and introduces sustainable burial cemetery models such as green cemetery and conservation burial grounds. The interdisciplinary literature review covers landscape architecture, urban planning, urban ecology, environmental sciences, and sustainable development research. The ecological memorial landscapes, which promote human biomass “return” back into biological cycles, could create ecosystems that merge into urban green infrastructure networks, and transform the end-of-life into an active mechanism for environmental preservation. City planners and landscape architects are uniquely positioned to promote this sustainable model by reimagining and zoning cemeteries as urban green infrastructure. This study suggests that despite legal, religious, and cultural barriers, the rise of eco burial practices signals a generational evolution and shift toward ecological accountability and “death positivity” movement.

items.titel: Environmental DNA (eDNA) applications for biodiversity monitoring across countries in the Sub-Saharan African region: a systematic review
items.samenvatting_bron: Introduction Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) contains highly diverse aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems but remains underrepresented in biodiversity research. Environmental DNA (eDNA) offers a non-invasive approach for biodiversity assessment, yet its application across SSA has not been comprehensively synthesized. Methods A systematic review following PRISMA 2020 was conducted using Google Scholar and Scopus for studies published from January 2018 to April 2026. Eligible peer-reviewed English-language studies used eDNA or DNA metabarcoding to assess aquatic or terrestrial biodiversity in SSA. Data were extracted on geographic distribution, ecosystems, target taxa, markers, sequencing platforms, sampling approaches, reference databases, and reported constraints. Results Twenty-five studies met the inclusion criteria. Aquatic ecosystems accounted for 88% of studies, while fish were the dominant target taxon (48%). Southern Africa had the largest geographic representation. The most frequently used marker was 12S rRNA (52%), and Illumina was the dominant sequencing platform (72%). Incomplete reference databases were reported as a major limitation in 68% of studies, while terrestrial and arthropod-focused applications were markedly underrepresented. items.titel: Machine Learning for Biodiversity Conservation: A Review of Ecological Monitoring, Species Prediction, and Conservation Applications

Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a valuable approach for processing large and complex ecological datasets, identifying species, predicting species distributions, monitoring ecosystem changes, and supporting conservation decision-making. items.titel: Contribution of eDNA Metabarcoding to Model Ecosystems: Case Study of Threatened Peri-Urban Mediterranean River

This targeted spatial snapshot captured aquatic, semi-aquatic, and terrestrial signals. items.titel: Marine Mammal Monitoring Research from 2014 to 2023: A Bibliometric Analysis of Collaboration, Technological Trends and Research Themes
items.samenvatting_bron: Marine mammal monitoring research has expanded considerably alongside developments in acoustic, remote-sensing, telemetry, molecular, and computational approaches. This study used bibliometric analysis to characterise the structure and evolution of research published between 2014 and 2023. A total of 2586 peer-reviewed publications retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection were analysed using CiteSpace to examine publication trends, collaboration networks, keyword co-occurrence, temporal clusters, and citation bursts. Annual publication output increased from 155 articles in 2014 to a peak of 362 in 2022, while collaboration networks revealed prominent research hubs across North America, Europe, Asia, and Oceania. Temporal and keyword analyses indicated increasing attention to machine learning, artificial intelligence, remote sensing, and environmental DNA, reflecting a broader movement towards automated and multimodal monitoring approaches. items.titel: Beyond Structural Barriers: Storytelling, Affect and Municipal Responsibility in Urban NBS Implementation
items.samenvatting_bron: Nature-based solutions (NBS) are valuable instruments for climate adaptation and resilience. Existing research on urban NBS barriers focuses mostly on structural and technical elements, while co-creation and local knowledge are regularly cited as critical for successful implementation. Even when barriers are easy to identify, a divide between ambition and reality generates procedural and knowledge gaps. This paper addresses this challenge through a case study of the Horizon Europe project URBREATH. Narrative inquiry is used to reveal invisible aspects of NBS implementation as experienced by city officials from Madrid, Cluj-Napoca, Leuven, and Tallinn. Drawing on storytelling workshops with city representatives and the authors’ participatory observation as project members, the paper shows that urban NBS are not only technical solutions, but also socio-cultural elements narrated through affective processes. We ask: what do city officials’ stories of difficult implementation moments reveal? Collected narratives show the personal commitment required to deliver urban nature-based solutions. Stories reveal that, in these cases, project managers absorbed institutional gaps informally, community participation was unevenly distributed, and hybrid NBS objects did not fit existing departmental categories. items.titel: Spatiotemporal Evolution and Driving Forces of Green Spaces in Shrinking Cities
items.samenvatting_bron: Urban shrinkage causes inefficient land utilization and landscape fragmentation. Green spaces are critical nature-based solutions for the sustainable development of shrinking cities, and play an important role in enhancing urban environmental quality and promoting residents’ physical and mental well-being. Using landscape ecological indices (PLAND, NP, and LPI) coupled with the spatial Durbin model (SDM), geographically weighted regression (GWR) and multiscale geographically weighted regression (MGWR), this study investigates the dynamics and influencing factors of green space in shrinking cities from 2000 to 2020. The results show that cities with population shrinkage experience the concurrent expansion and fragmentation of green spaces, cities with economic shrinkage demonstrate modest changes accompanied by low fragmentation, and cities with social shrinkage face a decline in green spaces with reduced patch numbers. The dynamics of green space are driven by the interplay of socioeconomic and natural factors, where the former operate at broader spatial scales and the latter exert localized influences. Consequently, spatial governance of urban green spaces should be implemented through multidimensional and multi-scalar coordinated strategies.

document.tekst_begin: Aanleiding In het Tweeminutendebat Ontwerp Natuurplan van 29 september 2026 is de motie Bromet ingediend met een drietal verzoeken betreffende de stedelijke ecosystemen en groen in de stad. Daarbij heeft de minister van Landbouw, Visserij, Voedselzekerheid en Natuur toegezegd dat u de Kamer een oordeel over deze motie zou doen toekomen. Geadviseerd besluit Bijgevoegde appreciatie te verzenden aan de Tweede Kamer. Kern De motie kan oordeel kamer worden gegeven. De appreciatie van de motie is afgestemd met B&E, VB en LVVN. Toelichting Dit najaar krijgen gemeenten inzicht in of de opgaven op hen van toepassing zijn en werken we met hen toe naar een optimale begrenzing van de stedelijke ecosysteemgebieden die kan worden opgenomen in het definitieve natuurplan. De stand van zaken daarop kan voor het eind van het jaar worden gecommuniceerd. Met de Handreiking Groen in en om Stad biedt het Rijk gemeenten en provincies nu al een werkwijze om afgestemd op de lokale omstandigheden doelen te bepalen en deze goed mee te nemen in lokaal beleid en projecten tot en met de uitvoering. document.tekst_begin: Aanleiding Op 11 september 2026 heeft u aan de Tweede Kamer een brief gestuurd over de voortgang van het voorstel Wet versterking waarborgfunctie Awb. De Tweede Kamer heeft deze brief geagendeerd voor het commissiedebat Grondrechten op 27 oktober 2026. De vaste commissie Binnenlandse Zaken heeft gevraagd om drie dagen voorafgaand aan dat debat een aantal feitelijke vragen te beantwoorden. Deze antwoorden - die u mede namens de StasJenV geeft - worden u bij deze nota ter ondertekening voorgelegd. StasJenV heeft inmiddels ingestemd met de beantwoording. Geadviseerd besluit U wordt geadviseerd bijgevoegde aanbiedingsbrief te ondertekenen. Kern • De Kamer stelt 41 feitelijke vragen. • De vragen gaan over de kosten van de verschillende onderdelen en over de verhouding tussen de doelstelling van het wetsvoorstel, de in de uitvoeringstoetsen begrote kosten en de gereserveerde middelen. Zonnepanelen helpen consumenten hun woonlasten te verlagen en geven de mogelijkheid bij te dragen aan de energietransitie. 40 procent van de woningen heeft al zonnepanelen. Het merendeel van huishoudens profiteert nu dus nog niet van elektriciteit die door de panelen op hun eigen dak is opgewekt. Om ook deze consumenten mee te kunnen nemen, moeten zij erop kunnen vertrouwen dat dit financieel aantrekkelijk is en blijft. Het bredere vertrouwen in de energietransitie loopt schade op nu zonnepanelen, die consumenten jarenlang werden aangeraden, door een wijziging in het overheidsbeleid onrendabel dreigen te worden. document.tekst_begin: Een slim energiesysteem met zon als basis Elektrische toepassingen gaan veel efficiënter om met energie dan fossiele verbranding, waarbij veel energie in de vorm van warmte verloren gaat. Daarom is kiest het Nationaal Plan Energiesysteem (NPE) ook voor elektrificatie als hoofdroute voor verduurzaming. Ook in de gebouwde omgeving is de keuze voor elektrificatie de juiste stap. Waar warmtenetten geen optie zijn vormen zonnepanelen, warmtepompen, elektrische auto’s, batterijen en energiemanagement samen één duurzaam en slim geheel. Door het elektriciteitsgebruik af te stemmen op het aanbod kunnen huishoudens en bedrijven meer van hun eigen zonnestroom benutten, hun energiekosten verlagen en het elektriciteitsnet ontlasten. Zo blijft verdere elektrificatie en verduurzaming ook bij netcongestie mogelijk. Beleid voor het stimuleren van zonne-energie moet zich daarom richten op het realiseren van opwek in combinatie met slimme afnametechnieken die eigen zonnestroom efficiënt benutten. Het vergroten van het eigen verbruik van zonnestroom vormt de basis voor de nieuwe businesscase voor zon op dak. Nederland heeft nog veel potentie om zon op dak te ontwikkelen. document.tekst_begin: Tweede Kamer der Staten-Generaal 2 Vergaderjaar 2025–2026 29 614 Grondrechten in een pluriforme samenleving Nr. 189 BRIEF VAN DE MINISTER VAN BINNENLANDSE ZAKEN EN KONINKRIJKSRELATIES Aan de Voorzitter van de Tweede Kamer der Staten-Generaal Den Haag, 19 augustus 2026 De vaste commissie voor Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport (VWS) heeft de Minister van VWS op 26 juni jl. verzocht te reageren op de petitie die u van de Stichting Evangelisatie Sjofar (de stichting) heeft ontvangen. Gelet op de verantwoordelijkheid voor grondrechten, waaronder de vrijheid van religie, stuur ik u de gevraagde reactie. Uit de brief die bij de petitie is ingediend, volgt dat de stichting zich zorgen maakt over onze samenleving. Zij concludeert dat de door haar geschetste problematiek in ons land mede het gevolg is van het feit dat onze overheid geen staatsreligie kent. De stichting roept de overheid dan ook op om zich te bekeren tot het Christendom en om het volk aan te sporen hetzelfde te doen. Aan het verzoek van de stichting aan de overheid om zich te bekeren tot het Christendom, en het volk aan te sporen hetzelfde te doen, kan ik geen gehoor geven. document.tekst_begin: Pagina 1 van 1 Aanleiding Het lid Van Houwelingen (FvD) heeft schriftelijke vragen gesteld over het bewijs naar Russische be- trokkenheid bij de drones in Leipzig en cyberaanvallen in Nederland. Geadviseerd besluit U wordt geadviseerd, mede namens de Minister van Binnenlandse Zaken en Koninkrijksrelaties, in te stemmen met het verzenden van de antwoorden aan de Tweede Kamer. Kernpunten • Het lid van Houwelingen (FVD) heeft gevraagd om bewijs naar de Kamer te sturen over Russische betrokkenheid bij drones die gesignaleerd zouden zijn bij Leipzig. • Daarnaast heeft het lid Van Houwelingen gevraagd om het bewijs dat Rusland verantwoordelijk is voor cyberaanvallen in Nederland naar de Kamer te sturen. • In algemene zin geldt dat de inlichtingen- en veiligheidsdiensten in het openbaar geen uitspraken doet over haar inlichtingenpositie, bronnen, en werkwijze. • Hiervoor geldt dat de Kamer via de geëigende kanalen geïnformeerd wordt, indien daartoe aanleiding is. • Ten aanzien van cyberaanvallen hanteren de inlichtingen-en veiligheidsdiensten het uitgangspunt om, waar mogelijk, hierover naar buiten te treden. Toelichting Financiële overwegingen Niet van toepassing. Juridische overwegingen

Bevingen waarvan we weten dat ze kunnen blijven voorkomen, maar die ons ook elke keer onaangenaam verrassen. Een beving die bij de bewoners in Groningen weer keihard binnenkomt. Het maakt ook opnieuw duidelijk hoe belangrijk de voortgang van de versterkingsoperatie is. Daarom valt het dilemma dat ik in deze brief schets mij des te zwaarder. Met deze brief informeer ik uw Kamer over de inzet van zelfstandigen bij de Nationaal Coördinator Groningen (NCG), de toepassing van de Wet Deregulering Beoordeling Arbeidsrelaties (DBA) en de mogelijke gevolgen daarvan voor de voortgang van de versterkings- operatie. Externe inhuur NCG NCG werkt met een combinatie van vaste medewerkers en externe capaciteit. items.titel: Neighbourhood Built Environment and Sense of Community in Tropical Residential Neighbourhoods: An Observation-Based Comparative Study in Malaysia
items.samenvatting_bron: The neighbourhood-built environment plays an important role in shaping social interaction and the development of a sense of community, particularly in rapidly urbanising tropical cities. While previous Malaysian studies have primarily used perception-based surveys, limited empirical attention has been given to the actual observation of physical neighbourhood features and their influence on social interaction and community cohesion. This study uses an observational analysis of two master-planned townships in Shah Alam, Selangor: Setia Alam and Bukit Jelutong, to evaluate the link between neighbourhood-built environment characteristics and a sense of community. A structured observation protocol was employed to assess eleven neighbourhoodbuilt environment attributes, including residential density, green infrastructure, architectural style, and recreational facilities, using a three point assessment scale. The findings indicate that although both neighbourhoods possess physical characteristics that support community development, they achieve these outcomes through different spatial planning approaches. Setia Alam scores in architectural, housing design excellence, and strong urban integration, promoting community identity and social interactions. Bukit Jelutong, on the other hand, benefits from lowered density, greater block sizes, and large green networks, which enhance spatial comfort and spontaneous social connections. items.titel: Lisbon
items.samenvatting_bron: This chapter examines how Lisbon’s climate‑neutrality agenda intersects with long‑standing socio‑spatial inequalities, housing precarity, and contested urban development paths. It reconstructs the historical and demographic trajectories that have shaped the Portuguese capital, highlighting the legacies of colonialism, touristification, and financialisation in producing uneven access to housing, mobility, and energy‑efficient dwellings. The chapter analyses the evolution of Lisbon’s climate governance architecture, from early commitments under the Covenant of Mayors to the Climate Action Plan 2030 and participation in the European Union’s mission for climate‑neutral and smart cities, focusing on the role of municipal departments, the energy and environment agency Lisboa E‑Nova, and an expanding ecosystem of open‑data platforms. It then explores how specific policies and projects in mobility, green infrastructure, water management, energy retrofitting, and the circular economy translate strategic visions into experiments on the ground, while also generating new distributive and procedural dilemmas. Particular attention is paid to forms of citizen participation and climate activism, including participatory budgeting, citizens’ assemblies, and climate‑justice movements, and to their ambivalent relationship with institutional initiatives.

items.titel: Construction of Dynamic Ecological Networks in Large-Scale Open-Pit Mining Areas on the Loess Plateau
items.samenvatting_bron: The Loess Plateau is a typical ecologically fragile area, where long-term intensive open-pit mining triggers severe vegetation loss, habitat fragmentation, and biodiversity decline. Although ecological network analysis integrating circuit theory and complex-network topology has become a mainstream connectivity assessment tool, existing studies mainly focus on urban agglomerations, nature reserves, and mountainous regions. Long-term dynamic networks considering mining and reclamation remain insufficiently understood in large coalfields. Taking the Pingshuo mining area as a case, this study combined MSPA, the MCR model, circuit theory, and complex-network approaches using remote-sensing images (1985, 1995, 2005, 2015, 2025), DEM, and road data to analyze 41-year spatiotemporal changes and propose a 2025 optimization plan. Ecological source proportion dropped from 6.17% (1985) to 3.56% (2015), then recovered to 9.79% (2025), dominated by forests and grasslands. Corridor length declined from 150.90 km to 99.32 km, and the 2025 network showed an average degree of 1.82 and an average path length of 1.45, indicating fragility. Under the proposed optimization scenario, node connectivity and network stability were projected to improve substantially. This study reveals how mining and restoration jointly shape ecological networks, offering a model-based theoretical framework for ecological security planning in similar fragile mining regions.

items.titel: Estimating absolute DNA abundance from replicated metabarcoding
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Datasets derived from mixed‐template DNA amplification and sequencing (‘metabarcoding’) are common in environmental DNA (eDNA), microbiome or microbial ecology analyses. Such metabarcoding data have been broadly used to inform estimates of biodiversity, distribution and abundance across a wide range of species and habitats. Generally, data from metabarcoding consist of a table of read‐counts assigned to each of a set of taxa or sequence variants. As such, they appear to contain quantitative information about the environment under study, immediately eligible for traditional community ecology analyses. In fact, metabarcoding data are compositional, can be biased by variation in PCR amplification rates among taxa, and have other statistical attributes that are distinct from many other common ecological observations. The difficulty in understanding and accounting for the complexity of metabarcoding observations has hindered their ecological interpretation and limited their integration with other ecological data types. items.titel: Synthesizing lessons from European adaptation pathways projects for climate resilience
items.samenvatting_bron: Climate adaptation planning faces challenges due to deep uncertainty and complex socio-ecological systems, often resulting in fragmented and incremental responses. This study synthesizes experiences from 21 cities and regions across eight European Union-funded projects, employing diverse methodologies to develop adaptation pathways that sequence climate adaptation measures over time. Through a systematic approach answering research questions across 8 themes to reveal lessons learned, we find varied stakeholder engagement approaches, data limitations influencing pathway quantification, inconsistent use of adaptation tipping points, and challenges integrating pathways with spatial and urban planning frameworks. While adaptation pathways enhance long-term strategic thinking and stakeholder collaboration, their institutional embedding and operationalization remain challenging within projects. Two main directions for future pathways research and practice are derived: (1) Embedding adaptation-pathway thinking into governance and planning; and (2) Addressing data needs, robust monitoring and multidimensional uncertainties. The study underscores the importance of flexible, inclusive, and data-informed approaches to support dynamic adaptation under uncertainty. items.titel: Diminishing cooling returns of urban greening amid a warming climate
items.samenvatting_bron: Urban greening is widely prioritized as a nature-based solution to mitigating intensifying heat extremes in the context of climate change, yet its long-term global efficacy remains inadequately quantified. Here we present a two-decade assessment of vegetation dynamics and associated cooling effects across 3,806 urban clusters worldwide, integrating multisource satellite observations with ground measurements from 4,855 meteorological stations. We identify a pronounced climate equity gap: While cities in the Global North have largely expanded green infrastructure, they exhibit cooling saturation with diminishing biophysical returns. Conversely, most cities in the Global South show vegetation stagnation or loss, compounding rapid warming trends. This asymmetry exposes a critical climate justice challenge, indicating that current greening efforts are insufficient to offset a warming trend. Our findings underscore the necessity for context-specific, integrated climate adaptation frameworks that address both the quantity and quality of urban vegetation to achieve equitable thermal resilience in an increasingly warm world.

items.titel: Hydraulic Modelling and Traditional Water Management for Nature-Based Flood Adaptation: A Spatial Planning Framework in the Lower Segura Basin (SE Spain)
items.samenvatting_bron: Flood adaptation in Mediterranean river basins requires approaches addressing floodwater circulation, redistribution and accumulation. This study proposes an exploratory spatial planning framework integrating two-dimensional hydraulic modelling, official flood hazard mapping and traditional water-management knowledge to identify potential Nature-based Solutions (NbS). Applied to the lower Segura basin (southeastern Spain), HEC-RAS 6.6 simulations used spatially uniform extreme rainfall to analyse water depths, velocities and the depth–velocity index (h·v). Functional hydraulic corridors were delineated using a threshold of h·v ≥ 0.30 m2/s. Comparison of simulated inundation with official SNCZI T500 mapping revealed 106.11 km2 of overlap (31.59%:, 182.42 km2 identified exclusively by the model (54.31%) and 47.34 km2 identified exclusively by SNCZI (14.09%). Qualitative spatial correspondence with traditional boquera irrigation systems and azarbe drainage networks informed a preliminary green infrastructure proposal combining multifunctional corridors, drainage adaptations and Controlled Storage Areas. The framework demonstrates the potential of integrating hydraulic modelling and historical knowledge into territorial flood adaptation planning. However, the simulations were not independently validated, and the hydraulic effectiveness of the proposed NbS remains unquantified.

items.titel: ECOLOGICAL CHALLENGES AND CLIMATE CHANGE IN TÜRKİYE: RISKS, SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT AND ADAPTATION STRATEGIES
items.samenvatting_bron: This article examines the principal environmental challenges facing Türkiye in the context of climate change and considers policy options for strengthening ecological security and sustainable development. Based on a qualitative review of international assessments and national climate policy documents, the study analyses water stress, drought, extreme heat, wildfires, floods, coastal risks, biodiversity loss and greenhouse-gas emissions. It discusses the relationship between climate vulnerability and economic sectors, particularly energy, agriculture, urban infrastructure and tourism. The analysis highlights the importance of combining mitigation measures with adaptation planning, including renewable energy, energy efficiency, integrated water management, climate-resilient agriculture, early-warning systems and nature-based solutions. Türkiye's 2024–2030 climate mitigation and adaptation plans provide an institutional framework, while implementation depends on coordination among national and local authorities, businesses and communities. The article concludes that an integrated, evidence-based approach can reduce climate risks while supporting economic resilience and a fair green transition.

items.titel: Coupled ecological pressures in urban environments: regional heterogeneity and drivers of carbon and water footprints
items.samenvatting_bron: A synergistic assessment of carbon and water footprints is essential for capturing the complexity of compound ecological pressures in rapidly urbanizing cities. However, their spatial distributions and integrated mechanisms at the district scale remain insufficiently explored and quantified. This study develops a spatially explicit analytical framework that integrates carbon and three types of water footprints (on-site blue water, runoff blue water, and road runoff gray water) with spatial autocorrelation and the Optimal Parameters-based Geographical Detector (OPGD) method. The analysis focuses on six central districts in Guangzhou, China, and evaluates spatial clustering patterns alongside the joint effects of natural and human drivers. The results reveal significant intra-urban clustering and a distinct core–periphery gradient in ecological footprints. This pattern is shaped primarily by urbanization intensity, human activities, and natural features, and interactions among these drivers generate marked nonlinear amplification. Consequently, ecological burdens are concentrated in densely populated and intensively developed districts, exacerbating spatial inequality and exposing specific areas to elevated environmental risks. Westnijlvirus WNV is een zoönotisch virus dat circuleert tussen wilde vogels (reservoir, brengen het dus niet over) en muggen (vooral Culex pipiens, de gewone huissteekmug). Ook mensen en paarden kunnen ziek worden na een beet van een besmette mug. Mensen en paarden kunnen het virus niet doorgeven en spelen geen rol in de verspreiding van het virus. Het virus kan niet direct van mens op mens worden overgedragen, overdracht door bloedtransfusie, orgaantransplantatie, prikaccidenten, en in de baarmoeder van moeder op kind is wel mogelijk. document.tekst_begin: De beweging naar een sterkere eerste lijn 2-meting ten behoeve van monitoring van het Integraal Zorgakkoord Ilgin Arslan Lisa Jansen Marloes Meijer Claudia Laarman Julia Simanowski Lilian van Tuyl Het Nivel levert kennis om de gezondheidszorg in Nederland beter te maken. Dat doen we met hoogwaardig, betrouwbaar en onafhankelijk wetenschappelijk onderzoek naar thema’s met een groot maatschappelijk belang. ‘Kennis voor betere zorg’ is onze missie. Met onze kennis dragen we bij aan het continu verbeteren en vernieuwen van de gezondheidszorg. We vinden het belangrijk dat mensen in staat zijn om deel te nemen aan de samenleving. Ons onderzoek draait uiteindelijk om de vraag hoe we de zorg voor de patiënt kunnen verbeteren. Alle onderzoeken publiceert het Nivel openbaar, dat is statutair vastgelegd. document.tekst_begin: De kwaliteit van de zorg bij Zorg en Jeugd Caribisch Nederland, afdeling Jeugdzorg Utrecht, maart 2026 Samenvatting Op 30 januari en 2 februari 2026 heeft de Inspectie Gezondheidszorg en Jeugd (verder: de inspectie) toezicht uitgevoerd bij Zorg en Jeugd Caribisch Nederland, afdeling Jeugdzorg (verder: Jeugdzorg). Doel van het toezicht was om te bepalen of Jeugdzorg verantwoorde vrijwillige ambulante jeugdzorg en jeugdbescherming verleent. De inspectie is bij haar onderzoek uitgegaan van de wettelijke bepaling dat de jeugdzorg in Caribisch Nederland van goed niveau is en in ieder geval veilig, doeltreffend, doelmatig en cliëntgericht wordt verleend en is afgestemd op de reële behoefte van de jeugdige. Daarnaast dient de verlening van verantwoorde jeugdzorg mede de systematische bewaking, beheersing en verbetering van de kwaliteit van jeugdhulp te omvatten. document.tekst_begin: Meer informatie: Paul van Beuzekom (06-10172854, pvbeuzekom@lto.nl) Position paper LTO Nederland rondetafelgesprek AMvB Dierwaardige veehouderij Dit position paper is tot stand gekomen in gezamenlijkheid met SBK, POV, NAJK en ZuivelNL en verwoordt de gedeelde aandachtspunten van deze partijen bij de AMvB Dierwaardige veehouderij. LTO Nederland onderschrijft de beweging naar een dierwaardige veehouderij. Maar de veehouderij kan dit niet alleen. Daarom hebben sector-, keten- en maatschappelijke partijen én de overheid het Convenant ‘Stappen naar een dierwaardige veehouderij’ gesloten. LTO vraagt de Tweede Kamer om vast te houden aan de afgesproken balans tussen AMvB, Convenant en Autoriteit. De AMvB moet de wettelijke ondergrens borgen en als ‘veegwagen’ fungeren; het Convenant is het realistische spoor om sneller en verdergaande stappen naar een dierwaardige veehouderij te zetten. Juist via het Convenant nemen alle partijen verantwoordelijkheid, van boer tot consument, en kan de markt zorgen voor de structurele financiering van hogere welzijnsstandaarden. document.tekst_begin: Position paper Rondetafelgesprek Algemene Maatregel van Bestuur (AMvB) Dierwaardige veehouderij Prof. Dr. Saskia S. Arndt, Hoogleraar Diergedrag Universiteit Utrecht, faculteit Diergeneeskunde Innovatie in de veehouderij vraagt ook om innovatie op het terrein van dierenwelzijn De zes leidende principes zoals die in 2021 door de Raad voor Dierenaangelegenheden (RDA) zijn geformuleerd, vormen samen een normatief en praktisch kader voor een dierwaardige veehouderij. Ze sluiten inhoudelijk aan bij het Five Domains Model van Mellor et al. (1994, 2015, 2016, 2020), dat aandacht besteedt aan voeding, leefomgeving, gezondheid, gedrag en de daaruit voortkomende mentale ervaringen van dieren. De RDA voegt daaraan een expliciet ethisch uitgangspunt toe: erkenning van de intrinsieke waarde en integriteit van het dier. Dit uitgangspunt bepaalt mede hoe mensen hun omgang met dieren behoren in te richten. Dierwaardigheid en dierenwelzijn hangen nauw samen. Binnen de dynamische benadering van dierenwelzijn kan (positief) welzijn worden beschreven aan hand van het vermogen van een dier om mentaal en fysiek adequaat te reageren op positieve en negatieve prikkels uit zijn interne en externe omgeving.

items.titel: Cave Monitoring Network and Long-Term Ecological Research in Portugal
items.samenvatting_bron: This document describes the Portuguese Cave Monitoring Network (CaveNet), a scientific infrastructure established within the framework of the EcoSub Chair. CaveNet provides an integrated framework for the quantitative monitoring of caves in Portugal, encompassing data collection, validation, processing and storage. The document presents the architecture and objectives of the infrastructure, highlights its scientific and ecological relevance and characterises the sites selected for Long-Term Ecological Research in Portuguese caves (LTER-Grutas). These sites host monitoring stations whose long-term environmental and ecological data are integrated into CaveNet. The document further discusses the advantages of an integrated cave monitoring network and its direct applicability to the assessment and reporting of the conservation status of habitat type 8310 - Caves not open to the public - under the Natura 2000 framework, as well as to the implementation of the Nature Restoration Regulation. In addition, CaveNet has significant socio-economic value, particularly in supporting the assessment and management of occupational risks associated with exposure to environmental hazards during underground work. In the longer term, the infrastructure will enable innovative research on carbon fluxes across the atmosphere–soil–subsoil–groundwater continuum, subsurface radioactivity emissions and the implications of subterranean processes for ecosystem services. items.titel: Sustainable development practices and SDG integration in brownfield redevelopment
items.samenvatting_bron: This chapter examines how sustainable development principles and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) can be systematically integrated into brownfield redevelopment to transform derelict and contaminated land into socially inclusive, environmentally restored, and economically productive urban assets. Drawing on the triple bottom line framework of environmental repair, economic viability, and social well-being, the chapter demonstrates how brownfield reuse inherently advances multiple SDGs simultaneously from improved public health and clean water to climate action, decent work, and sustainable cities. It reviews the international, European, and UK policy frameworks that drive sustainable brownfield practice, including the EU Green Deal, the National Planning Policy Framework, and associated funding mechanisms. Innovative and eco-friendly remediation techniques spanning bioremediation, phytoremediation, in-situ chemical treatment, nature-based solutions, and circular material reuse are evaluated for their sustainability credentials. The chapter further addresses adaptive reuse of existing structures, climate-resilient design, green infrastructure integration, and the social imperatives of community engagement, affordable housing, economic inclusion, and environmental justice. items.titel: Does the climate-adaptive city pilot policy exacerbate urban sprawl? Evidence from a quasi-natural experiment in China
items.samenvatting_bron: Although climate-adaptive policies are primarily designed to enhance urban resilience, they may also generate unintended consequences for urban spatial development. However, the impacts of climate-adaptive governance interventions on urban sprawl remain underexplored. Results show that pilot policy significantly promotes urban sprawl, a conclusion validated by robustness tests. items.titel: Why Do Goitered Gazelles Cross the Path of an Approaching Moving Object Instead of Fleeing?
items.samenvatting_bron: Animal–vehicle collisions are an important conservation concern. Although many studies examine road mortality and wildlife crossings, less is known about ungulates that run across the path of an approaching vehicle rather than simply fleeing. This study describes this behavior in goitered gazelles (Gazella subgutturosa) and examines its association with four recorded factors: approach category, group size, group composition, and month. In a forward stepwise logistic regression, approach category was associated with crossing behavior (Wald = 22.784, df = 2, p < 0.001). The odds of crossing were higher in the high-category group than in the low-category group (odds ratio = 2.36). However, the categories also differed in object type (cars, motor scooters, and bicycles/pedestrians), so the independent effect of speed cannot be separated from the effect of object type. Group size, group composition, and month did not meet the model’s entry criteria. These observational results identify an association, but do not determine whether path-crossing is a uniquely anti-predator response, a reaction to limited assessment time, or another form of behavior.

items.titel: On-site metabarcoding analysis of environmental DNA samples
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Environmental DNA metabarcoding is a powerful monitoring tool for assessing aquatic biodiversity, as well as the sustainability and impacts of fisheries and aquaculture. However, conventional laboratory workflows remain time-consuming and dependent on dedicated infrastructures. Here, we present a field trial of a fully portable, off-site eDNA metabarcoding pipeline that enables end-to-end analysis within a few days using compact equipment, including a BentoLab workstation and an Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) MinION sequencer. The workflow was implemented during two international training courses in Norway and Brazil, where students and early career researchers collected environmental samples, extracted and amplified DNA, prepared DNA libraries, and sequenced on-site before performing bioinformatics and statistical analyses. In the case study detailed here, seven eDNA samples collected and analysed on-site in the Oslofjord allowed detection of 16 fish and elasmobranch species. Although overall diversity was lower than in earlier studies using Illumina-based sequencing, our protocol reliably detected key species and demonstrates that portable eDNA metabarcoding is feasible for rapid ecological assessment, surveillance of high-risk regions and/or deployment in remote or resource-limited settings.

items.titel: Waterborne eDNA metabarcoding of the upper Llano River watershed (Texas, USA) detects regionally unreported green plant taxa
items.samenvatting_bron: Environmental DNA (eDNA) represents a promising preliminary tool for efficiently assessing biological diversity in locales where conducting intensive field surveys is logistically challenging, as in the case of west-central Texas. Its utility for characterizing biodiversity across broad spatial scales is amplified in lotic systems, which can transport eDNA several kilometers from its source and often contain signals from both aquatic and nearby terrestrial organisms. In the present study, we employed waterborne eDNA metabarcoding to broadly characterize regional green plant (Viridiplantae) diversity in two west-central Texas rivers, the North Llano River and the South Llano River, that constitute the upper reaches of the ecologically and economically important Llano River watershed. We detected taxa from 45 green plant families, encompassing both streptophytes and chlorophytes. Among these, 18 taxa had not been previously documented in the study area, representing putative novel distributional data pending direct field observations. Additionally, we assessed the influence of three methodological factors—sequencing depth, PCR template volume, and volume of water filtered—on detected diversity. Collectively, our findings highlight the value and limitations of eDNA metabarcoding for broad-scale biodiversity characterization and provide insights into the potentially unrecognized floristic diversity of understudied Texas rivers.

items.titel: Achieving Good Quality of Coastal Waters: The Role of Policy Coherence across the Land–Sea Interface
items.samenvatting_bron: Coastal ecosystems are affected by pressures from both land and sea. Ensuring good ecosystem conditions therefore requires ecosystem-based management (EBM) that addresses pressures at their source, regardless of where they originate. The EU Water Framework Directive and Marine Strategy Framework Directive both employ EBM approaches. Yet despite their complementary aims, they fall short of enabling holistic source-to-sea management. Incoherences in scope, scale, and legal force hinder achieving their environmental objectives, while sectoral economic policies often prevail. Case studies from Norway, Finland, and France illustrate varied national responses to these design challenges in EU law. Despite their efforts, none of the cases achieved good coastal water quality. Revisions of EU legislation and policy are needed. Coherence in objectives and measures should be strengthened across the Directives, enabling clearer and better coordinated roles; procedural alignment should reduce duplication and enhance synergies; and stronger legal and financial steering is needed to influence sectoral policies.

items.titel: Cities with birdsong: the impact of forest city designation on bird biodiversity
items.samenvatting_bron: Nature-based solutions such as forest cities are emerging as effective approaches for achieving symbiosis between humans and other species within urban environments. This article centers on China’s National Forest City Designation (NFCD) policy and develops a framework to investigate its impact on biodiversity. This article tests this framework with two key tools: a novel dataset of large-scale birdwatching data from China and a difference-in-differences approach. Research findings reveal that the NFCD policy has spurred a 5.6%−8.0% rise in bird biodiversity, and the regular inspection mechanism guarantees the sustainability of this impact. Increased forest area, improved forest quality, and enhanced forest protection are the primary association mechanisms. Further analysis indicates that NFCD provides greater protection for non-endangered birds, larger-bodied birds, forest-dwelling birds, and resident birds. The NFCD policy yields better results in urban areas as well as regions administered by officials who are younger, better educated, or possess relevant experience. These findings provide novel insights into how tournament-style policies impact urban landscapes and biodiversity.

items.titel: Wetland plant biodiversity in China: a scoping evidence map linking ecosystem services, SDGs, and governance instruments
items.samenvatting_bron: Wetlands are biodiversity hotspots and critical nature-based solutions for water purification, climate regulation, and flood and coastal risk reduction, yet they remain among the world’s most threatened ecosystems. This scoping review synthesized 2,482 China-focused studies published between 2001 and 2026 to examine how wetland plant biodiversity supports ecosystem services and informs governance and United Nations. Multidimensional biodiversity, including taxonomic, compositional, functional, and phylogenetic attributes, was consistently linked to water-quality regulation, carbon sequestration, habitat provision, and flood protection. Major pressures included land conversion, hydrological alteration, pollution, coastal reclamation, invasive species, and climate change. Although few studies explicitly referenced SDGs or named policy instruments, substantial evidence supported SDG 6, 13, 14, and 15. Synthesized within a State–Function–Pressure–Response framework, the findings demonstrate that conserving wetland plant biodiversity is essential for sustaining ecosystem services and strengthening biodiversity-informed wetland governance in China.

items.titel: Decoupling hydraulic and treatment optima in floating treatment islands: implications for nature-based solutions in stormwater systems
items.samenvatting_bron: Floating treatment islands (FTIs) are increasingly deployed as nature-based solutions (NbS) in urban stormwater systems. However, conventional design relies on empirical hydraulic proxies, lacking a physics-based framework that integrates multi-scale flow processes with localized reaction kinetics. This study presents a technical increment by quantifying the 3D multi-scale coupling between system-scale hydrodynamics and localized root-zone pollutant uptake using validated computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of a full-scale stormwater pond. The results reveal a clear physical decoupling between hydraulic and treatment optima. Hydraulic efficiency, governed by flow redistribution and short-circuiting mitigation, associated with improved flow distribution and reduced short-circuiting, is maximised at a root-length-to-pond-depth ratio (LR/DP) of approximately 0.50. Conversely, FTI pollutant mass removal – driven by local advective flux and residence time within the porous root matrix – reaches an individual maximum near LR/DP ≈ 0.65, with the upstream island achieving 52% removal. Crucially, system-scale pollutant removal plateaus beyond LR/DP = 0.50 (62% at both 0.50 and 0.65), as flow blockage by deep upstream roots induces hydraulic shielding over downstream structures. Consequently, LR/DP ≈ 0.50 represents a robust, physics-informed design optimum, maximizing water quality benefits while preserving hydraulic performance, structural stability, and cost-efficiency.

items.titel: Transformações no uso e cobertura da terra e seus reflexos socioambientais em uma bacia hidrográfica periurbana de Campo Grande – Mato Grosso do Sul
items.samenvatting_bron: Disordered urbanization, characterized by excessive soil sealing, inadequate structural interventions, and effluent discharge, results in severe water degradation, a scenario historically observed in Campo Grande − Mato Grosso do Sul. In this context, this study analyzed the socio-environmental impacts of urbanization and macro-drainage works in a peri-urban watershed in the northern zone of the city. The methodology integrated the analysis of geotechnical maps, cartographic materials, the MapBiomas historical series (1985–2024), and fieldwork. The results demonstrated a drastic alteration in the landscape: the urbanized area jumped from 12.70% in 1985 to 42.72% in 2024, reducing native vegetation to only 13.06%. Rapid urban growth on fragile soils (Entisols - Quartzipsamments), combined with unfinished interventions, intensified erosive processes and generated high socio-environmental costs. Macro-drainage works received millions in public investments but failed to mitigate the impacts. In the Cônsul Assaf Trad Park, a stalled construction project left an environmental liability characterized by active erosion, silted reservoirs, and a dam rupture in 2019. Obstruction of the riverbed by construction waste and clandestine sewage connections was also observed. It is concluded that the lack of urban planning exacerbated the environmental fragility of the watershed, making the adoption of Nature-based Solutions imperative for the recovery and ecological restoration of the area.

Integrated conservation of linear heritage landscapes from a biocultural diversity perspective: A case study of the Huizhou-Hangzhou Ancient Trail, China
items.samenvatting_bron: by Yuanliang Dong, Chengcheng Pan, Siyu Pan, Lei Zhang Linear cultural heritage landscapes embody the long-term coupling relationships between ecological processes and human cultural practices, yet conservation models guided by a single ecological or cultural goal fail to meet their holistic management needs. Based on the perspective of biocultural diversity, this study takes the Huizhou-Hangzhou Ancient Trail (HHAT) as a case study and constructs a comprehensive conservation framework oriented toward spatial planning. Biodiversity and cultural diversity patterns are assessed and their spatial relationships are quantified using the coupling coordination degree model. The biocultural diversity index is further integrated with the Marxan systematic conservation planning model to identify Biocultural Core Protected Areas (BCCPA) and support differentiated spatial conservation strategies. The results indicate that biodiversity and cultural diversity along the HHAT exhibit a pronounced antagonistic coupling relationship: regions with antagonistic coupling account for 98.90% of the total study area, while coordinated regions make up only 0.02%. Based on the natural and cultural context of the study area, this pattern may be jointly influenced by rigid competition for small‑scale spatial resources, the dual effects of traffic corridors, and the cumulative effects of traditional livelihood activities. document.tekst_begin: 1 Netwerktoets voorjaarsbesluitvorming klimaat 2026 Context Een van de maatregelen uit het IBO Bekostiging Elektriciteitsinfrastructuur is dat het Rijk de netbeheerders zal betrekken bij beleidsvoorstellen die naar verwachting een grote impact zullen gaan hebben op het energiesysteem (stroomlijnen besluitvorming). Een van de manieren waarop dat kan, is de netwerktoets bij nieuw beleid. Door het uitvoeren van de netwerktoets wordt bereikt dat de Rijksoverheid vroeg in de beleidsvorming inzicht verkrijgt in de verwachte effecten van het beleid op het energiesysteem, de energie-infrastructuur, infra-investeringen en op afnemers, bijvoorbeeld de positie van afnemers in congestie-/congestiegevoelige gebieden. Dit ondersteunt beleidsmakers bij het vormgeven van doelmatig, uitvoerbaar en stelselconsequent transitiebeleid. De afgelopen periode is door een werkgroep van de netbeheerders met een representatie van vanuit de ministeries KGG, Financiën en het Klimaat- en energiefonds gewerkt aan het vormgeven van de netwerktoets. items.titel: Spatio-Temporal Dynamics of Urban Heat Islands and Sustainable Urban Development in a Rapidly Urbanizing Tropical City
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Rapid urbanization in tropical cities is intensifying surface urban heat island (SUHI) effects, posing significant challenges for sustainable urban planning. Hence, the present study investigates the spatio-temporal dynamics of land surface temperature (LST) and its relationship with vegetation and built-up indices in Raipur district, India, between 2015 and 2025. The multi-temporal Landsat imagery processed on the Google Earth Engine (GEE) was used to derive normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), normalized difference built-up index (NDBI), and LST, followed by SUHI intensity assessment and correlation analysis. The results reveal a clear spatial pattern in which urban and peri-urban areas exhibit elevated LST values, while vegetated rural zones act as thermal buffers. The NDVI-LST showed a consistent negative correlation (− 0.51 to − 0.33), highlighting the cooling role of vegetation, whereas LST-NDBI showed a consistent strong positive correlation (0.76–0.82), highlighting the warming impact of impervious surfaces. Change detection analysis indicates declining vegetation cover in peri-urban zones and expansion of built-up areas, contributing to outward propagation of thermal hotspots. Although SUHI intensity showed a relative decline over time, this was primarily driven by rising rural temperatures rather than urban cooling, suggesting regional thermal homogenization. items.titel: WILDLIFE UNDERPASSES AS INTEGRATED CIVIL AND ECOLOGICAL INFRASTRUCTURE: A Conceptual Design Framework for Highway Connectivity
items.samenvatting_bron: This report, titled “Wildlife Underpasses as Integrated Civil and Ecological Infrastructure: A Conceptual Design Framework for Highway Connectivity,” examines the integration of civil engineering principles and ecological considerations in the conceptual planning of wildlife underpasses along highways. The report discusses wildlife–vehicle collisions, habitat fragmentation, wildlife-crossing infrastructure, underpass planning and design considerations, drainage and hydraulic requirements, structural and geotechnical considerations, construction practices, maintenance, monitoring, and environmental management. It presents a conceptual framework intended to support safer wildlife movement and improved ecological connectivity across transportation infrastructure. The report is based on a review of relevant literature and published guidance. It is a conceptual technical study and does not claim original field surveys, site-specific investigations, or experimentally validated structural designs. Actual implementation would require site-specific ecological assessments, geotechnical investigations, hydraulic analysis, structural design, and approval by the relevant authorities. items.titel: Ag/Ti Electrodes for Electrochemical Nitrate Reduction: Revealing Highly Effective Interfaces by In‐Situ Electrochemical Mass Spectrometry
items.samenvatting_bron: The electrochemical reduction of nitrate to hydroxyl amine or ammonia is a prominent means to effectively valorize agricultural effluent emissions. We demonstrate that bimetallic electrodes, composed of Ag nanoparticles deposited on Ti metal, exhibit a pronounced synergy in nitrate reduction in acidic electrolyte. This is evidenced by in‐situ electrochemical mass spectrometry (EC‐MS), showing NO evolution in a complex potential‐dependent profile at lower onset potentials compared to single metal Ag or Ti electrodes. Furthermore, liquid phase analysis shows a significant Faradaic efficiency to hydroxylamine for Ag/Ti electrodes, even at potentials above 0 V RHE , i.e., requiring at least a 200–300 mV lower overpotential than necessary for the single metal electrodes. We discuss favorable NO and hydroxylamine formation to be occurring on highly effective Ag/Ti interfaces. This work highlights the importance of interfaces and suggests that optimization of (Ag/Ti) bimetallic electrodes appears to be a valuable means to develop high performance electrodes for the reduction of nitrate in acidic conditions.

items.titel: Multiscenario Simulation and Prediction of Urban Green Space in the Changle District of Fuzhou City, China, Based on Multiobjective Optimization and a GeoSOS-FLUS Model
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Green spaces in densely urbanized areas along China’s southeast coast generally face spatial competition between ecological protection and development intensity, as well as conflicts between policy-oriented and market-driven values. Among them, Changle District in Fuzhou City, as the core area of the coastal new city, needs to coordinate its green space system to address complex three-dimensional problems. To explore the optimal configuration of green spaces under different ecological constraints and achieve a balance between ecological, economic, and social benefits, this paper takes Changle District in Fuzhou City as the research area, with 2020 as the base year, and innovatively combines a multiobjective optimization model with the Geographic Simulation and Optimization System–Future Land Use Simulation (GeoSOS-FLUS) model. The former is used to balance multiple objectives such as ecological conservation, economic development, and social needs, generating optimal allocation schemes. The latter precisely simulates the dynamic evolution of green spaces based on these schemes. Together, they overcome the limitations of traditional models, which cannot account for economic and ecological benefits when simulating complex urban land use. Based on this model combination, this paper simulates and predicts the area structure, spatial configuration, and target benefits of green space in Changle District in 2030 under ecological high-, medium-, and low-constraint scenarios.

By comparison, routine environmental DNA (eDNA) research generally uses non-invasive sampling to infer species presence and characterise biological communities from mixed genetic material. Evolving genomic technologies are expanding the information recoverable from both tissue-based and environmental samples, making sample source alone an insufficient indicator of intended use, information sensitivity, or potential for resource utilisation. items.titel: Tracking the evolution of urban resilience: A systematic review of research themes and trends over two decades
items.samenvatting_bron: Urban resilience has become central to global urban policymaking as cities confront growing challenges from climate change, disasters, and socio-economic disruptions. However, research in this field spans multiple disciplines and perspectives, leaving insights fragmented across a vast body of literature. Here we provide the most comprehensive synthesis to date, analyzing over 1400 documents during 2000–2023 to trace its evolution, identify key themes, and highlight future research directions. We show that urban resilience research spans 96 countries, but over 60% comes from China, the USA, the UK, and the Netherlands. Priorities also vary due to differing development contexts.
